Rashi on Arakhin 3a:10:1.hebrew: והצרוע - משמע צרוע אחרינא, לרבות את האשה:
Rashi on Arakhin 3a:10:1.english: And the leper - [This] implies another leper, to include a woman.

Rashi on Arakhin 3a:11:1.hebrew: א"כ למה נאמר איש לענין שלמטה - דמשמע איש ולא אשה, ולאו אטמא יטמאנו קאי, דהתם אפי' אשה; אלא אקרא דלמטה קאי, דמשתעי בפריעה ופרימה:
Rashi on Arakhin 3a:11:1.english: If so, why is "a man" stated? Regarding the matter below - For [the word "man"] implies a man and not a woman, and it does not refer to "he shall surely pronounce him unclean," for there [it applies] even to a woman; rather, it refers to the verse below, which speaks of letting [the hair] grow loose and rending [the garments].

Rashi on Arakhin 3a:12:1.hebrew: הכל רואין והכל כשרים לראות - חדא הוא, ולא גבי הדדי תניא:
Rashi on Arakhin 3a:12:1.english: "All inspect" and "all are fit to inspect" - They are one [and the same teaching], and they were not taught together [in a single baraita].

Rashi on Arakhin 3a:12:2.hebrew: שאינו בקי - והולך תלמיד חכם ישראל ורואה עמו, ואומר לו: "אמור טמא" — והוא אומר; "טהור" — והוא אומר — שהטומאה והטהרה תלויה במאמר הכהן. והכי תניא בת"כ:
Rashi on Arakhin 3a:12:2.english: [A priest] who is not expert - And an Israelite Torah scholar goes and inspects with him, and says to him, "Say: Impure," and he says [it]; [or,] "Pure," and he says [it] — for [the status of] impurity and purity is dependent upon the declaration of the priest. And so it is taught in Torat Kohanim.

Rashi on Arakhin 3a:13:1.english: But didn't the Master say - [This is stated] in the first chapter of Shevuot (6a).

Rashi on Arakhin 3a:13:2.english: [Where] they explain to him and he understands - The laws of afflictions.

Rashi on Arakhin 3a:14:1.english: To sanctify - To mix spring water with the ashes of the sin-offering. The reasoning of the Rabbis and Rabbi Yehuda is explained in tractate Yoma, in the chapter [entitled] "Taraf BaKalpi" (Yoma 43a).

Rashi on Arakhin 3a:15:1.english: An uncircumcised person - [One] whose brothers died on account of circumcision.

Rashi on Arakhin 3a:15:2.english: Who sprinkled - From the purification water onto the impure [person].

Rashi on Arakhin 3a:15:3.hebrew: הזאתו כשרה - טעמא מפרש ביבמות בפ' הערל (יבמות דף עב:): מידי דהוה אטבול יום, שפסול בתרומה וכשר בפרה:
Rashi on Arakhin 3a:15:3.english: His sprinkling is valid - The reason is explained in Yevamot, in the chapter [entitled] He'arel (Yevamot 72b): [It is] just as it is with a tevul yom [one who immersed that day], who is disqualified from terumah but is qualified for the [red] heifer.

Rashi on Arakhin 3a:16:1.hebrew: תרי "הכל שוחטין" איכא בפרק קמא דחולין (דף ב. ודף טו:):
Rashi on Arakhin 3a:16:1.english: There are two [mishnayot of] "Everyone slaughters" in the first chapter of Chullin (2a and 15b).

Rashi on Arakhin 3a:17:1.english: All compel [others] to ascend - [This is stated] in the last chapter of Ketubot (110b).

Rashi on Arakhin 3a:1:1.hebrew: לאתויי נשים - שחייבות במקרא מגילה, וכשרות לקרותה ולהוציא זכרים ידי חובתם:
Rashi on Arakhin 3a:1:1.english: To include women - [To teach] that they are obligated in the reading of the Megillah, and are fit to read it and discharge men of their obligation.

Rashi on Arakhin 3a:2:1.hebrew: מזמנות לעצמן - שלש נשים, וכן שלשה עבדים. אבל אין שתי נשים או שני עבדים מצטרפין עם (שני) אנשים, לפי שיש באנשים מה שאין בנשים ובעבדים — שאין הנשים אומרות "ברית", ואין העבדים אומרים "על נחלתנו":
Rashi on Arakhin 3a:2:1.english: [Women] form a zimmun for themselves - [This means] three women, and likewise three slaves. But two women or two slaves do not combine with (two) men, because there is in men that which is not in women and in slaves — as women do not say "covenant," and slaves do not say "for our inheritance."

Rashi on Arakhin 3a:4:1.english: Any man - "When he has a discharge from his flesh, etc." (Leviticus 15:2).

Rashi on Arakhin 3a:7:1.hebrew: מכרת - (דכרת): דהאי קרא בנכנס טמא למקדש כתיב, ומחייב ליה כרת; ולהכי כתיב "איש" למעוטי קטן, דלאו בר עונשין הוא. אבל טמא הוא, לטמא אוכלין ומשקין כגדול:
Rashi on Arakhin 3a:7:1.english: From excision - (Of excision): For this verse is written concerning one who enters the Sanctuary while impure, and it renders him liable to excision; and for this reason it is written "a man," to exclude a minor, for he is not subject to punishment. But he is impure, to impart impurity to food and drink like an adult.

Tosafot on Arakhin 3a:10:1.hebrew: והצרוע - משמע צרוע אחרינא לרבות את האשה. א"כ למה נאמר איש לענין שלמטה? "איש", דמשמע ולא אשה — לאו א"טמא יטמאנו" קאי, דהתם אפילו אשה, אלא אקרא דלתחת קאי, דמשתעי בפריעה ופרימה — ל"ה. ואע"ג דבנגעי ראש וזקן כתיב (ויקרא יג) "אשה", לא ילפינן מינה, דהתם איצטריך, דאע"ג שאין רגילות לצמח שיער בזקן האשה, מטמאה. ויש להקשות: אמאי לא נפקא לן אשה מ"אדם", דמשמע אשה במקום קטן, דכתיב (במדבר ל״א:ל״ה) "ונפש אדם", וכיון דשקולים הן — ויבאו שניהם? וי"ל, דסד"א: מדאיצטריך קרא לרבויי אשה בנגעי (קטן) [זקן], מכלל דשאר נגעים ליכא לטמאות אשה אם לא מן הפסוק. וקשה: הוה ליה לרבויי אשה [מאדם], ו"איש" למעוטי קטן מפריעה ופרימה, "והצרוע" לרבות קטן לטומאה? וי"ל, דמסתברא למעוטי פריעה ופרימה מאשה, שגנאי הוא זה:
Tosafot on Arakhin 3a:10:1.english: "And the leper" - [This] implies another leper, to include a woman. If so, why is "a man" stated with regard to the matter below? "A man," which implies [a man] and not a woman, does not apply to "he shall surely pronounce him impure," for there even a woman [is included]; rather, it applies to the verse below, which speaks of letting [the hair] grow loose and rending [garments] — [this is] the wording of the Kunteres [Rashi]. And even though regarding afflictions of the head and beard it is written (Leviticus 13) "a woman," we do not derive [other afflictions] from it, for there it was necessary [for Scripture to state explicitly], because even though it is not usual for hair to grow on a woman's beard, she becomes impure. And one may raise a difficulty: Why do we not derive [the inclusion of] a woman from "a person" [adam], which implies a woman instead of a minor, as it is written (Numbers 31:35) "and human persons"; and since they are equally balanced, let both of them come [and be included]? And it can be answered: For I would have thought that since Scripture needed to include a woman in afflictions of (a minor) [the beard], it follows by implication that in other afflictions, a woman cannot be rendered impure unless from [an explicit] verse. And it is difficult: [Scripture] should have included a woman [from "a person"], and [used] "a man" to exclude a minor from letting [hair] grow loose and rending [garments], and "and the leper" to include a minor for impurity? And it can be answered: It is reasonable to exclude letting [hair] grow loose and rending [garments] from a woman, because this is a disgrace [for her].

Tosafot on Arakhin 3a:12:1.hebrew: הכל רואין, הכל כשרין לראות - חדא הוא, ולאו גבי הדדי תניא:
Tosafot on Arakhin 3a:12:1.english: "Everyone may inspect, everyone is fit to inspect" - They are [actually] one [and the same teaching], and they were not taught next to each other [in a single source].

Tosafot on Arakhin 3a:13:1.english: "But didn't the Master say" - [This is stated] in the first chapter of Shevuot (daf 6a).

Tosafot on Arakhin 3a:13:2.hebrew: דמסברי ליה וסבר - הלכות נגעים. "שאינו בקי" — והולך ת"ח ורואה עמו: הוא אומר "טמא" והוא אומר "טמא", שהטומאה והטהרה תלויה באמירת כהן, והכי תניא ליה בת"כ — ל"ה. והתם בת"כ איתרבו ישראל, מדכתיב: "או אל אחד". ומסקינן התם: מאחר שסופו לרבות ישראל, למאי הלכתא כתיב "כהן"? שאין טומאה וטהרה אלא מפי כהן, שאפי' כהן שוטה רואה נגעים. אע"ג דמסברי ליה וסבר, מקרי ליה "כהן שוטה", שאינו בקי בפני עצמו. ועי"ל: "דמסברי ליה וסבר" דהכא לאו אכהן קאי, אלא אישראל חכם דקאי גביה — מסברי ליה וסבר. וא"ת: פשיטא! מה לי מלמדין מאתמול, למלמדין אותו היום? וי"ל: דאע"ג שאינו בקי אלא באותו נגע — כשר לראות:
Tosafot on Arakhin 3a:13:2.english: "Where they explain to him and he understands" - [This refers to] the laws of leprous marks. [And regarding the Gemara's statement,] "One who is not an expert" [Rashi explained]: And a Torah scholar [talmid chakham] goes and inspects with him; he [the scholar] says: "Impure," and he [the priest] says: "Impure," for ritual impurity and purity are dependent upon the pronouncement of a priest, and so it is taught in Torat Kohanim — [this is] the wording of the Kunteres [Rashi]. And there in Torat Kohanim, Israelites were included [as fit to inspect leprous marks], from that which is written: "Or to one [of his sons the priests]" (Leviticus 13:2). And we conclude there: Since ultimately [the verse] comes to include an Israelite, for what halakha was "priest" written? That ritual impurity and purity are only from the mouth of a priest, so that even a foolish [i.e., inexpert] priest may inspect leprous marks. [And] even though they explain to him and he understands, he is called a "foolish priest" because he is not an expert on his own. And furthermore, one can say that "where they explain to him and he understands" here does not refer to the priest, but rather to the wise Israelite who stands beside him — [it is referring to a case where] they explain to him and he understands. And if you will say: It is obvious! What difference does it make to me whether they taught [him] yesterday or they teach him today? And one can say: [It teaches] that even though he is an expert only in that [particular] mark, he is fit to inspect [it].

Tosafot on Arakhin 3a:14:1.hebrew: לקדש - לערב מים חיים באפר חטאת. טעמייהו דרבי יהודה ורבנן מפרש בפרק טרף בקלפי (יומא מג.):
Tosafot on Arakhin 3a:14:1.english: "To sanctify" - [This means] to mix spring water with the ashes of the purification offering [the red heifer]. The reasons of Rabbi Yehuda and the Rabbis are explained in chapter Taraf BaKalpi (Yoma 43a).

Tosafot on Arakhin 3a:15:1.hebrew: ערל - שמתו אחיו מחמת מילה, שהזה ממימי חטאת על הטמא — הזאתו כשרה. טעמא מפרש ביבמות פרק הערל (יבמות דף עב:): מידי דהוה אטבול יום, שפסול בתרומה וכשר בפרה. ומצי לאיתויי ברייתא דתניא התם הכי בפירוש, אלא דר' אלעזר שגורה בפי כל יותר:
Tosafot on Arakhin 3a:15:1.english: "An uncircumcised male" - [This refers to one] whose brothers died on account of circumcision, who sprinkled from the purification water upon the [ritually] impure person — his sprinkling is valid. The reason is explained in Yevamot, chapter HaArel (Yevamot 72b): Just as it is with a tevul yom [one who immersed that day], who is disqualified from terumah and fit for [the rite of the red] heifer. And [the Gemara] could have cited the baraita that is taught explicitly there, but rather [the statement] of Rabbi Elazar was more fluent in everyone's mouth.

Tosafot on Arakhin 3a:16:1.hebrew: תרי הכל שוחטין - בפ"ק דחולין (דף ב ודף טו:):
Tosafot on Arakhin 3a:16:1.english: "Two [mishnayot of] 'Everyone slaughters'" - [Are] in the first chapter of Chullin (2a and 15b).

Tosafot on Arakhin 3a:17:1.english: "All may compel [others] to ascend" - [This is taught] in Ketubot, the last chapter (folio 110b).

Tosafot on Arakhin 3a:1:1.hebrew: לאתויי נשים - שחייבות במקרא מגילה, וכשרות לקרות ולהוציא זכרים ידי חובתן — ל"ה. אבל בה"ג לא פסק הכי, ומביאין ראיה מן התוספתא, וזה לשונם: "הכל חייבין בקריאת מגלה כו'; טומטום ואנדרוגינוס חייבין, ואין מוציאין הרבים ידי חובתן; אנדרגינוס מוציא מינו, ואינו מוציא את שאינו מינו; טומטום אינו מוציא לא את מינו ולא את שאינו מינו; מי שחציו עבד וחציו בן חורין אינו מוציא לא את מינו ולא שאינו מינו; נשים ועבדים וקטנים פטורין מקריאת מגילה" — עד כאן לשון התוספתא. וההלכות גדולות הוסיפו: "אלא שחייבין בשמיעה, לפי שהכל היו בספק להשמיד להרוג ולאבד":
Tosafot on Arakhin 3a:1:1.english: "To include women" - [That is,] that they are obligated in the reading of the Megillah, and are fit to read [it] and discharge males of their obligation — [this is] the wording of the Kunteres [Rashi]. However, the Bahag [Ba'al Halakhot Gedolot] did not rule this way, and they bring proof from the Tosefta, and this is their wording: "All are obligated in the reading of the Megillah, etc.; a tumtum [a person of indeterminate sex] and an androgynos [a hermaphrodite] are obligated, but do not discharge the public of their obligation; an androgynos discharges his own kind, but does not discharge [one who is] not of his kind; a tumtum discharges neither his own kind nor [one who is] not of his kind; one who is half-slave and half-freeman discharges neither his own kind nor [one who is] not of his kind; women, slaves, and minors are exempt from the reading of the Megillah" — until here is the wording of the Tosefta. And the Halakhot Gedolot added: "Rather, they are obligated in hearing [the Megillah], because all were in doubt [i.e., in peril of]: 'To destroy, to slay, and to annihilate' [Esther 3:13]."

Tosafot on Arakhin 3a:1:2.hebrew: (פסק): ר' יהושע הוה מכנס כל אנשי ביתו וקורא לפניהם; רבי יונה, אבוה דרבי מנחם, היה מתכוין לקרותה לפני נשים שבביתו, שהכל היו בספק והכל חייבין בשמיעה — עד כאן לשון הלכות גדולות. לכך צריך לפרש בכאן, דאין הנשים מוציאין אלא נשים, אבל אנשים — לא; ו"הכל חייבין במקרא מגילה" כו' — לאיתויי נשים [שמוציאין נשים אחרות]. והוה מצי למימר: לאיתויי קטן, אליבא דרבי יהודה דמכשיר בקטן בפרק שני דמגילה (דף יט:):
Tosafot on Arakhin 3a:1:2.english: (Ruling): Rabbi Yehoshua would gather all the members of his household and read [the Megillah] before them; Rabbi Yonah, the father of Rabbi Menachem, would intend to read it before the women of his household, for all were in doubt [i.e., in danger of destruction], and all are obligated in hearing [it] — until here is the wording of the Halakhot Gedolot. Therefore, it is necessary to explain here that women discharge [the obligation of] only women, but men — no [they do not]; and "All are obligated in the reading of the Megillah, etc." — [comes] to include women [who discharge the obligation of other women]. And [the Gemara] could have said: To include a minor, according to Rabbi Yehuda, who validates [the reading of] a minor in the second chapter of Megillah (folio 19b).

Tosafot on Arakhin 3a:2:1.hebrew: מזמנות לעצמן - שלש נשים, וכן שלשה עבדים; אבל שתי נשים אין מצטרפין (לשני) [עם] אנשים, לפי שיש באנשים שאין בנשים ובעבדים: שאין הנשים אומרות "ברית", ועבדים אין אומרים "על ארץ שהנחלת לאבותינו". וצ"ל: דרשות הוא לנשים לזמן, אבל חיובא ליכא. ותדע, מדקא מייתי מיניה סייעתא למ"ד בפ' שלשה שאכלו (ברכות מה:) דנשים אם רצו לזמן מזמנין, משום דמאה נשים כתרי גברי; ואם היו חייבות, א"כ קשיא ליה, דהא "רצו לזמן" קאמר. ועל זה סמכו נשים שלנו שאינן מזמנות:
Tosafot on Arakhin 3a:2:1.english: "[Women] form a zimmun for themselves" - [This means] three women, and likewise three slaves [may form a zimmun among themselves]. However, two women do not combine (with two) [with] men, because there is [an element] in men that is not in women and in slaves: for women do not recite [the mention of] "covenant" [brit milah in the Grace after Meals], and slaves do not recite "for the land that You gave as an inheritance to our fathers" [as they have no portion in the Land of Israel]. And it must be said that it is optional [reshut] for women to form a zimmun, but there is no obligation [chiyuv]. And know [that this is so], from [the fact] that [the Gemara] brings support from it for the one who said in chapter Sheloshah She-Akhlu (Berakhot 45b) that regarding women, if they wished to form a zimmun they may form a zimmun, because a hundred women are like two men; and if they were obligated, if so, it would be difficult for him, for behold, it states "they wished to form a zimmun"! And upon this our women relied, that they do not form a zimmun.

Tosafot on Arakhin 3a:3:1.hebrew: לאתויי קטן היודע למי מברכין וכדרב נחמן כו' - ואמר נמי בברכות (דף מח.): "ולית הלכתא ככל הני שמעתא אלא כדרב נחמן" וכו'. ואפילו הכי לא קי"ל כוותיה, אלא כדאמר רבי יוסי בירושלמי: "כמה זימנין אכלית עם אבא חלפתא ועם חביבי, ולא זמנין עלי עד שהבאתי ב' שערות":
Tosafot on Arakhin 3a:3:1.english: "To include a minor who knows to Whom one recites a blessing, and in accordance with Rav Naḥman, etc." - And [the Gemara] also says in Berakhot (48a): "And the halakhah is not in accordance with all those statements, but rather in accordance with Rav Naḥman," etc. And even so, we do not hold in accordance with him, but rather as Rabbi Yose said in the Yerushalmi: "How many times did I eat with my father Ḥalafta and with my uncle, and they did not include me in a zimmun until I brought [forth] two [pubic] hairs!"

Tosafot on Arakhin 3a:4:1.hebrew: דתניא איש כי יהיה זב וגו' - והא דלא מייתי מתניתין דיוצא דופן (נדה מג:), דתנן: "תינוק בן יום אחד מטמא בזיבה" — משום שהברייתא מפרש יותר:
Tosafot on Arakhin 3a:4:1.english: "As it is taught: 'When any man has a discharge, etc.'" - And that which [the Gemara] does not cite the Mishnah in [chapter] Yotzei Dofan (Niddah 43b), where we learned: "A one-day-old infant becomes impure through zivah" — [it is] because the baraita explains [it] more [fully].

Tosafot on Arakhin 3a:7:1.hebrew: למעוטי קטן מכרת - דהאי קרא בנכנס למקדש טמא כתיב, ומחייב ליה כרת; ולהכי כתיב "איש" למעוטי קטן, דלאו בר עונשין הוא; אבל טמא הוא לטמא אוכלים ומשקין כגדול. ויש לתמוה: למה לי קרא לפוטרו, כיון דלא מצינו קטן נענש? וכן קשה פרק ד' מיתות (סנהדרין נב:): "איש כי ינאף" — פרט לקטן. ומיהו התם י"ל, דמשום קלון האשה יתחייב, דומיא דבהמה הנרבעת. ושמא איצטריך, דסד"א: הואיל ונתרבה לטומאה, יתחייב כרת — קמ"ל דלא:
Tosafot on Arakhin 3a:7:1.english: "To exclude a minor from karet" - For this verse is written regarding one who enters the Sanctuary [while] impure, and makes him liable to karet [spiritual excision]; and therefore "a man" is written, to exclude a minor, who is not subject to punishment. But he is [nevertheless] impure [so as] to defile food and drink like an adult. And there is reason to wonder: Why do I need a verse to exempt him, since we do not find that a minor is punished? And it is similarly difficult in chapter Arba Mitot (Sanhedrin 52b): "A man who commits adultery" — to exclude a minor. However, there it can be said that [one might have thought] he should be liable on account of the woman's disgrace, similar to an animal that was copulated with. And perhaps [here] it was necessary, for you might have thought: Since he was included regarding impurity, he should [also] be liable to karet; [therefore] it teaches us that [this is] not [so].
